options.title: The Panama Canal runs on rain. What if it stops?
options.first_line: The Panama Canal runs on rain. So what if the rain stopped?
options.first_frame: The map of Panama with the canal cutting across it, ships queued at both ends and a rain cloud over the big lake in the middle, the rain thinning.

options.title: Panama Canal out of water: who waits first?
options.first_line: Panama's canal is running short of water. Who waits first if it dries up?
options.first_frame: Ships lined up at both ends of the Panama Canal on the map, the lake in the middle shrinking, a queue growing at each end.

options.title: Why can't the Panama Canal work without rain?
options.first_line: Without rain, the Panama Canal stops. So what if it never rained there again?
options.first_frame: The canal across Panama on the map, its lake turning from blue to cracked mud as a ship halts in the middle.

why: The title asks a how-is-that-possible question (why would a sea canal need rain?) that only the video answers, and the first frame of the lake cracking to mud under a halted ship reads with the sound off.
